clue.text: Live on own and stay out of trouble

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece sitting on another is placed above it, so the first piece comes before the second

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
to own something is to have it

explanation.surface: Advice to someone moving into their first place alone: keep your nose clean.
explanation.definitionFit: To behave is to conduct yourself well and avoid getting into mischief or difficulty.

clue.text: Remote island, very behind, gets broadband at last

parts.note: I is the standard abbreviation for island
so means very, as in so tired
running behind schedule is being late

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word just before it, the only part kept

parts.note: the final letter of broadband

explanation.surface: A far-flung island, behind the times, is finally connected to fast internet.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhere remote is far away and cut off, which is exactly what an isolated place is.

clue.text: Blight that is overshadowing New Jersey's old city

indicators.note: to overshadow is to loom over and envelop, so the first piece wraps around what follows

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is
the US postal abbreviation for New Jersey
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A sinister shadow falls over an ancient New Jersey town.
explanation.walkthrough: Ur, in ancient Mesopotamia, is the setter's favourite old city; the surface wants a New Jersey town instead.
explanation.definitionFit: To blight something is to spoil or damage it, the verb sense matching harm or wound.

clue.text: Primarily, flat earth's associated with the Netherlands and part of East Anglia

indicators.note: things associated with each other are joined together, so the pieces are simply set side by side
primarily means in the first place, so only the opening letters of the following words are used

parts.note: the first letters of flat and earth
NL is the international code for the Netherlands
taken as written

explanation.surface: Flat-earth thinking is linked to the low, level Dutch landscape and eastern England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' looks like it joins two halves of the clue but is a letter source; the definition is only the last four words.
explanation.definitionFit: The Fens are the flat drained marshland region of eastern England covering parts of Cambridgeshire, Norfolk and Lincolnshire.

clue.text: One quiet look by doctor gives confidence

parts.note: a means one, as in a single
p, piano, is the musical marking for quiet
lo is an old word for look or behold
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A calm, unhurried examination by the GP is reassuring.
explanation.definitionFit: Aplomb is self-assured poise, the composure that comes with being sure of yourself.

clue.text: American soldier's in trouble for slow movement

indicators.note: in puts the preceding pieces inside the word that follows

parts.note: ado is fuss or bother
A is a standard abbreviation for American
GI is a US army private

explanation.surface: A US serviceman is disciplined for dawdling on the march.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' suggests marching soldiers, but it is a section of a piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Adagio is the musical term for a slow tempo, and so names a slow section of a symphony or sonata.

clue.text: Courier has difficulty getting green transport

parts.note: a mess is a difficult or confused situation

indicators.note: to transport is to carry off somewhere else, so these letters are moved into new places

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A delivery rider struggles to find an eco-friendly vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green transport' reads as an electric van or bike; transport is really the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A courier carries letters and parcels, the job of someone who delivers messages.

clue.text: Picked up sterilised tool

indicators.note: picked up means heard, as a radio picks up a signal, so the word's sound matters

parts.note: a spayed animal has been sterilised

explanation.surface: Someone lifts a garden implement that has been disinfected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' and 'tool' suggest lifting a spade; 'sterilised' means neutered here, not cleaned.
explanation.definitionFit: A spade is a digging implement with a flat blade, one of the commonest garden tools.

clue.text: Everyone in company's posh and devious with no sensitivity

indicators.note: in places the first word's letters inside the word that comes next

parts.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company
all means everyone
U means upper-class, as opposed to non-U
sly means cunning or devious

explanation.surface: A smart, scheming firm where all the staff are cold-hearted.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class comes from the old British U and non-U labels for posh and common usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting callously means behaving in a hard-hearted way, showing no feeling for others.

clue.text: Wife's naughty dog takes last of pie in one big chunk

parts.note: W is the standard abbreviation for wife

indicators.note: something naughty misbehaves, so the following letters do not stay in line

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: last of keeps only the final letter of the following word

parts.note: the final letter of pie

explanation.surface: The family dog misbehaves and wolfs a pie in one gulp.
explanation.walkthrough: A wodge is informal British English for a thick lump of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A wodge is a large, thick lump or mass, such as a hefty slab of cake or bundle of papers.

clue.text: Astonish with crazy climbing

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing reads a word from the bottom upwards

parts.note: nuts means mad or crazy

explanation.surface: Wow the crowd with an insane ascent of a cliff.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun someone is to shock or amaze them so much they are left speechless.

clue.text: Kind of information outlet

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, as in a figure being out, so the letters after it are jumbled

parts.note: read as out plus let: the second half supplies the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A sort of news source or media channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of' reads as 'a sort of'; Kind is the definition and outlet splits into an indicator and three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Kind and gentle are both adjectives describing a soft, caring and considerate manner.

clue.text: Jotter only available in printed version?

parts.note: surface reading: a book that has no digital edition
setter's reading: split the answer into a denial followed by the word for an electronic book

explanation.surface: A notepad you cannot download, only buy on paper.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as NOT E-BOOK: something that is not an electronic book exists only in print.
explanation.definitionFit: A jotter is a small pad or exercise book for writing quick notes in.

clue.text: Ignoring odd bits of wordier poem

indicators.note: ignoring the odd-numbered letters leaves only the second, fourth and sixth ones

parts.note: the even letters of wordier

explanation.surface: Cutting the strange parts out of a long-winded verse.
explanation.definitionFit: An ode is a lyric poem addressed to or praising a subject, such as Keats's to a nightingale.

clue.text: Legend from space, perhaps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the table explaining the symbols on a map
second meaning: the space bar is one example of a button on a keyboard

explanation.surface: A myth that came from outer space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legend' and 'space' suggest science fiction; one is a map's explanation panel and the other a keyboard button.
explanation.definitionFit: A map's legend lists what its symbols mean, and the space bar is one of the buttons you press when typing.

clue.text: Little fish in river's following daughter's line in current

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the first piece named goes at the end
the second in places the pieces before it inside the word after it

parts.note: a tide is a current of the sea
D is the abbreviation for daughter
L is the abbreviation for line
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A tiny fish swims in a river after a girl's fishing line drifts in the stream.
explanation.walkthrough: D and L sit inside TIDE to make TIDDLE, and R comes after. Tiddler is everyday British for a small fish such as a minnow.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiddler is a very small fish, the kind children catch in nets from streams.

clue.text: Thanks housemaid heartily coming in with drink

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so the selected letter goes inside the other piece

parts.note: ta is informal British for thanks

indicators.note: heartily points to the heart of the preceding word, its central letter

parts.note: the middle letter of housemaid

explanation.surface: Gratitude to the maid, who arrives warmly with a cuppa.
explanation.walkthrough: E goes inside TA to make T-E-A.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea is the hot beverage brewed from leaves, Britain's everyday drink.

clue.text: Mother's Day morning

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for day
a.m. denotes the morning

explanation.surface: The morning of the annual celebration of mums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mother's Day' looks like one phrase; Mother is the definition and the possessive is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A dam is the female parent of an animal, used especially of horses and livestock.

clue.text: Ring section from multiple choice

indicators.note: a section from a phrase is a run of its letters taken across the word boundary

parts.note: the end of multiple running into the start of choice

explanation.surface: A circle cut from an exam question with several options.
explanation.definitionFit: Ring as a verb means resound or reverberate, which is what a repeated sound does.

clue.text: Tension of a new team yet to play

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to play means to move about freely, so the preceding letters are rearranged

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new
a cricket or football team is an eleven, XI in Roman numerals
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Nerves in a freshly formed side that has not played a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yet to play' reads as not yet having played; it is the word yet followed by the signal to rearrange it.
explanation.definitionFit: Anxiety is a state of nervous worry and unease, the strain felt before a test.

clue.text: On paper the irony's wasted

indicators.note: wasted means ruined or drunk, so these letters are in a sorry, disordered state

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A sardonic remark about written arguments that are lost on readers.
explanation.definitionFit: Something true on paper holds only as a plan or theory, not necessarily in practice.

clue.text: Dress for retirement party outside with jacket top when worn by old lady

indicators.note: something worn by a person surrounds them, so the first piece wraps around the next
outside points to only the outer letters of the word before it

parts.note: the first and last letters of party

indicators.note: top means the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: the first letter of jacket
as means when, as in as I left
ma is informal for mother, one's old lady

explanation.surface: An elderly woman chooses an outfit for a leaving do, with a smart jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retirement party' looks like a leaving do; retirement here means going to bed, and party is a letter source.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyjamas are what you wear when you retire for the night, i.e. go to bed.

clue.text: Gangster's power with young is massive

parts.note: Al Capone is the stock crossword gangster
might means power or strength
Y is the abbreviation for young

explanation.surface: A mobster's hold over the youth is enormous.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, almighty means very great or huge, as in an almighty row.

clue.text: Left relative briefly with companion in a boat

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter of the word before it is dropped

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
an aunt is a relative
CH, Companion of Honour, is a British order

explanation.surface: Abandoned briefly by family, someone sits in a boat with a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A launch is a large motorboat, used for example to ferry people in a harbour.

clue.text: Eventually popular issue comes up

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: to issue is to emit or give out

explanation.surface: Sooner or later a trendy topic surfaces.
explanation.definitionFit: In time means after a while, or in the end, the same as eventually.

clue.text: Director of a vast production incorporating any number

indicators.note: incorporating means taking into the body, so one letter goes inside the rest
a production is something created or staged, so these letters are put together in new form

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
n stands for any number in maths

explanation.surface: The filmmaker behind a huge production with a cast of countless extras.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Director' and 'production' suggest film; the director here is the in-car device telling you where to go. Satnav is British for a GPS unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A satnav gives a driver turn-by-turn directions, so it directs the route.

clue.text: Admirer has diamonds, maybe, and gold!

parts.note: diamonds are one example of a card suit
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A wooer arrives bearing diamonds and gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitor is a man courting a woman, someone who admires and pursues her.

clue.text: Knowing when to express disapproval on a point

parts.note: as means when
to tut is to click the tongue in disapproval
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Being savvy about when to object on a particular issue.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowing as an adjective means shrewd and perceptive, just as an astute person is.

clue.text: Races in to purchase a sandwich

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the word that follows

parts.note: to buy is to purchase
the TT is the Isle of Man motorcycle races, Tourist Trophy

explanation.surface: Someone dashes into a shop to grab a sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: A butty is northern English for a sandwich, as in a chip butty.
explanation.definitionFit: Butty is informal British English for a sandwich, typically a filled roll or slice of bread.

clue.text: Party's policy statement has nothing obvious up front

indicators.note: up front puts the piece just before it at the start, ahead of the other one

parts.note: manifest means plain or obvious
O resembles zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A party's pledges lack any clear opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nothing obvious up front' reads as nothing clear at the start; really 'obvious' goes up front and 'nothing' follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A manifesto is the published declaration of a political group's aims and plans before an election.

clue.text: Rogue president's behind swindle

indicators.note: behind means coming after, so the first piece named goes at the end

parts.note: a scam is a swindle
P is the abbreviation for president

explanation.surface: A crooked head of state is the mastermind of a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' tempts you towards RUMP, a word for a backside, but nothing fits; here it only places the president's letter after the swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: A scamp is a mischievous rascal or roguish person, often said fondly of a child.

clue.text: Make a virtue of love

indicators.note: to make is to construct, so the following letters are built into a new word

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The proverbial advice to turn love into something good, like making a virtue of necessity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' looks like part of the idiom but is in the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A favourite is a darling or person most cherished, as one might call a sweetheart my love.
